messages:
junaid (support): Acme Integrations on Dedicated reported intermittent 401s from their private LB -> L7 proxy -> Redwood gateway chain. They only see failures when their SSO cookie and an Authorization header are present. Happening ~5% of requests. Raising to infra to help repro and root cause. Customer transcript + logs below.

Acme Integrations (customer): We started seeing this yesterday after upgrading haproxy to 2.4. Calls from our backend to Redwood sometimes return 401: "missing token". We only call with `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (short) and a large `_sso` cookie (30kb). Happens under load, not every request.

marta (eng-infra): Thanks — can you paste the raw request and an example failing response? Also which LB in front (AWS NLB / ALB / internal)?

Acme Integrations (customer): NLB (internal) -> haproxy (L7) -> istio ingress -> redwood private gateway. Failing request example (redacted):

```
POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
Authorization: Bearer eyJ...REDACTED...
Cookie: _sso=VERY_LONG_BASE64_PAYLOAD... (≈30kb)
Connection: keep-alive
Content-Type: application/json
Content-Length: 512
```

Response: `401 Unauthorized` with body `{\"error\":\"missing authorization header\"}`. Envoy ext_authz show: `authorization: \"Bearer eyJ...REDA\"` (truncated).

tyler (eng-platform): Truncated in ext_authz log suggests the header gets split or partially forwarded. Could be header fragmentation across TCP segments with some proxy rewriting or haproxy config that extracts fields. Do you see any `http-request set-header` rules in haproxy?

junaid (support): Customer pasted haproxy config snippet:

```
frontend fe_http
  bind *:80
  mode http
  option httplog
  # they do a field extraction to normalize Authorization
  http-request set-header Authorization %[req.hdr(Authorization),field(2)]
  default_backend be_app
```

(They claim this existed prior to 2.4 upgrade but behavior changed after).

marta (eng-infra): Ah — `field(2)` will split on whitespace and pick the second token. For `Authorization: Bearer <token>` that returns the token only, fine. But if the header is broken into two TCP segments mid-header (e.g., long cookie triggers segmentation), `req.hdr(Authorization)` can be incomplete, and `field(2)` may return empty or truncated token. Also some haproxy versions changed how `req.hdr()` reads multi-line/truncated headers.

Acme Integrations (customer): Is there a way to reproduce? We can run a loop from our backend to try to trigger it.

tyler (eng-platform): Try a tight loop with keep-alive on, and a large Cookie value to force segmentation. Example quick repro (bash):

```
for i in {1..500}; do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED_TOKEN" \
    -H "Cookie: _sso=$(head -c 30000 /dev/urandom | base64)" \
    -H "Connection: keep-alive" \
    https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate &
  sleep 0.01
done
```

They should see a few 401s in the stream. If you re-run with `-H 'Connection: close'` the failures should disappear.

Acme Integrations (customer): Ran that loop — reproduced ~12/500 failed (401). Switching to `Connection: close` -> 0/500.

marta (eng-infra): OK this nails connection reuse + large header size as the root condition. Short-term mitigation: remove the `field(2)` transform and forward the header unchanged, or change haproxy to use `http-request set-header Authorization %[req.hdr(Authorization),regsub(^\s+|\s+$,\,)]` (safer) or simply stop manipulating Authorization header at L7. Also `option http-server-close` or `option http-keep-alive` tweaks can change segmentation behavior.

junaid (support): Customer tried `http-request set-header Authorization %[req.hdr(Authorization)]` (no `field(2)`) — reran repro -> failures dropped to 0/500. They reverted that haproxy change and reported stable.

tyler (eng-platform): For our docs and private deployment guidance we should: 1) call out that `Authorization` header rewriting/extraction can break under large combined header sizes; 2) recommend avoiding opaque `field()` extraction on auth headers; 3) add a note about `Connection`/keepalive interactions with NLB/TCP segmentation. I'll open an eng-infra ticket to add a section to Dedicated/Private docs.

marta (eng-infra): Also adding a small detection snippet to console telemetry: if we see ext_authz logs where `authorization` header length < 10 but client sent header present, flag it as `header-truncation-suspected`. That helps catch customers with broken L7 proxies.

incidents-bot: Jira ticket created: INFRA-4721 (add docs + detection for auth header fragmentation).

junaid (support): Customer happy with workaround and will schedule a haproxy upgrade to remove the risky transform. They asked if Redwood Gateway can be made more tolerant — currently ext_authz rejects empty or truncated token with 401. Any chance of returning 400 + hint?

tyler (eng-platform): We intentionally return 401 for auth fail. But we can add better debug logging (only in non-prod) that includes header lengths and a short hint. I'll file a small RFC with opt-in debug on private control planes.

marta (eng-infra): Next steps summary: (1) Support confirmed repro and mitigation with customer. (2) Customer will remove `field(2)` transform and enable `http-server-close` for now. (3) Eng-platform to update Dedicated docs + add detection. (4) Eng-runtime to investigate opt-in verbose header diagnostics.

Acme Integrations (customer): Thanks all — will confirm next week after we roll the change. :white_check_mark:

junaid (support): Marking this thread resolved for now, will reopen if customer reports regressions.
